title: Harden and simplify Pearl Catcher 26.1.2
objective: Import the reviewed Pearl Catcher 2.5.1 source as a first-class project and make catch execution fail-closed, vanilla-faithful, latency-aware, ownership-safe, behaviorally tested, and simpler to maintain without replacing the proven general solver architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Low-robustness or insufficient-clearance catch plans are rejected rather than executed, including previously accepted zero-percent robustness cases
Legit hotbar/offhand input leases have bounded confirmation deadlines and cannot permanently block later catches
Observed pearls and wind charges are attributed to the local player using vanilla projectile ownership before becoming attempt-owned
Preflight safety covers vanilla-relevant block, world-border, and hittable-entity interference and fails closed for unmodeled fluid or environmental projectile dynamics
Delayed catch timing accounts conservatively for network/server projectile age and refuses plans whose timing uncertainty exceeds the safe collision window
Silent execution restores server rotation after the final projectile action without corrupting projectile inherited movement ordering
Legit right-click execution cannot silently become a block or entity interaction; ambiguous interaction contexts fail closed
Automatic slot/offhand restoration never overwrites a newer manual player choice and all owned asynchronous state is removed on disable, cancellation, disconnect, or supersession
Unsupported riding or vehicle movement states fail closed until their exact vanilla send-position semantics are modeled

CatchExecutor responsibilities are reduced into focused coordination, vanilla-input, and projectile-tracking components without introducing alternate planner architectures or extra user-facing tuning clutter
Behavioral regression tests cover every reviewed failure mode, existing physics/solver regressions remain green, and CI verifies build plus tests
The initial synchronous solver hot path is profiled and pruned where safe, with no correctness regression and no arbitrary asynchronous complexity
